findings.statement: The supplied evidence is a single saved HTML snapshot of a ChatGPT conversation interface; it does not represent a full site crawl.
The static page contains navigation, main-content, header, and aside containers with extensive button and SVG markup.
Twelve script elements are present: one external JavaScript reference, ten executable inline scripts, and one application/json data element.
An inline appearance bootstrap checks theme preferences and browser color-scheme signals and refers to locally cached appearance configuration.
Twenty-five linked stylesheets and fourteen inline style elements are present, with visible light and dark appearance tokens.
The static DOM includes 102 buttons, 131 inline SVG elements, and 127 aria-label attributes; interactive behavior and accessibility quality remain unverified.
The standalone HTML points to a missing companion resource directory containing CSS, JavaScript, and image references. This limits source-level analysis of those dependencies.
The captured document includes account-linked and conversation-related state; raw values, full serialized data, and source excerpts must not be published.
Four inline scripts interact with a React Router stream controller to enqueue or close serialized route-loader data. Some payload-bearing scripts contain private state, which was not published.

React streaming boundary replacement helpers occur in three script elements and are consistent with streamed server-rendered content. The saved file does not prove successful hydration or runtime rendering.
One early bootstrap script references sessionStorage and location fragments for a transient launch workflow; these data are environment-specific and were not captured in public outputs.
Root attributes identify a Codex Linux desktop browser capture context, so the observed UI structure should not be generalized to all ChatGPT browser environments.
Four file-type input elements are present, including three with multiple-selection attributes and one with a capture attribute. Successful upload behavior was not tested.
The inline CSS contains four @media rules: two reduced-motion rules, one hover-related rule, and one width-related rule. External stylesheets remain unavailable.
The snapshot has fifteen anchor elements; this does not establish the site's full route graph, which requires broader capture scope.

The saved DOM has seventy aria-expanded attributes, five aria-controls attributes, and 108 data-state attributes. These describe static accessibility/state hooks and do not verify runtime transitions.

Fifteen anchor elements appear in the saved markup. Fourteen references use HTTP(S) absolute addresses, one is a fragment, and three links specify a new-tab target with noreferrer/noopener relationship flags.

The saved inline CSS contains 497 custom-property declarations (including repeats), 261 CSS var() references, fourteen keyframes, three @layer occurrences, and 104 elements with inline style attributes. None establishes the complete styles of the missing CSS files.

The standalone document contains 31 external references in six resource categories, documented by safe ordinal rather than source path. Referenced files were not supplied and are not present in the repository.

The executable inline script code contains no fetch(), XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket constructor, or EventSource constructor reference in this capture. This is not evidence that the full application makes no network requests.

The DOM has 147 aria-hidden, 127 aria-label, 70 aria-expanded, five aria-controls, five aria-live, and 29 tabindex attributes. Static markers do not demonstrate keyboard accessibility or correct runtime transitions.

The saved markup includes script nonce attributes, referrer metadata, and a sandbox attribute on one iframe. Three new-tab links include noopener/noreferrer; no effective CSP headers or runtime policy were inspected.

The saved document carries one referenced application script and ten inline executable scripts, along with 25 linked stylesheets and inline styles; loading performance cannot be measured from the source alone.

The observed page architecture combines streamed route-loader state, streamed React DOM boundary handling, inline appearance initialization, a styled application shell, and referenced client assets. The missing bundle prevents definitive framework-module and event-flow reconstruction.

Static page inspection covers the available markup, inline scripts, inline styles, and external resource references; it cannot verify unprovided bundles, executed interactions, remotely served contracts, whole-site routing, or site-wide performance.

limitations: The input is a single HTML document from an authenticated session; it is not a representative whole-site crawl.
The saved-page companion directory was not supplied, so referenced stylesheet, JavaScript, and image file contents are unavailable.
One large embedded application/json payload may contain account-linked or conversation content and was not copied into public artifacts.
DOM markup and source references do not prove live behavior, remote API responses, backend implementation, browser compatibility, or security properties.
The capture date is not independently established by server evidence; processed_at records the local specimen intake.
First internal version: no previous capture exists for comparison.
A static DOM does not prove button actions, event-handler connections, form submission, upload support, or keyboard navigation. This limits the interaction-model task.
Missing external script source prevents a trustworthy module graph and remote-service contract reconstruction.
No request waterfall, timing data, server response headers, authenticated API execution, or runtime instrumentation was available for this capture.
The ordinal external-reference inventory avoids publication of raw resource paths and embedded state.
Internal snapshot status reviewed means static evidence was assessed and bounded; it is not an assertion that the full website is understood.
